chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated to us, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Ibn Abi 'Umayr, from Hammad ibn 'Uthman, from Hafs al-Kinasi, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him):

"What is the minimum that makes a servant a believer?" He said: "He testifies that there is no god but Allah, and that Muhammad is His servant and Messenger, and he acknowledges obedience and recognizes the Imam of his time. When he does that, he is a believer."
ai.seo_question: What are the minimum conditions for a person to be considered a believer in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Ma'ani al-Akhbar* delineates the four pillars of faith in Shia theology: Tawhid, Nubuwwah, Imamah, and Ma'ad (implied by obedience). It emphasizes that true belief is not merely verbal but requires the specific recognition (*Ma'rifah*) of the living Imam of the time, linking doctrinal belief directly to spiritual authority. This underscores the Shia view that obedience to the Imam is an intrinsic component of faith, distinct from mere monotheistic declaration.
